questions.q: According to Oracle's security design guideline, where should grants (privileges and data security policies) actually attach?
options: Directly to the user account
Directly to the job role
To the duty role
To the abstract role only
questions.explain: The design guideline is that grants are made to duty roles, which are then given to job or abstract roles as children.

options: A set of related tasks performed as part of a job
A synonym for a job role
A report listing every user's access
A single, real-world action on a single business object
questions.explain: A privilege is the smallest grantable unit — one specific action, like 'void a payment,' on one business object.

questions.q: Reading the access chain from the bottom up, what is the correct order?
options: User → job role → duty role → privilege
Privilege → duty role → job or abstract role → user
Duty role → privilege → user → job role
Job role → privilege → duty role → user
questions.explain: Access traces from a privilege, held by a duty role, held by a job or abstract role, which is provisioned to a user.

questions.q: A user at Castellan Robotics can't perform a specific action. What is the correct way to fix it?
options: Trace which duty role should carry that privilege, confirm the job role includes it, and confirm the job role is provisioned to the user
Add the missing privilege directly to the user's account
Delete the user's account and recreate it
Grant the user every available job role to be safe
questions.explain: Because privileges attach to duty roles (not users), fixing access problems means tracing the chain: privilege → duty role → job role → provisioning, not patching the user directly.

questions.q: Why can one duty role inherit other, more granular duty roles?
options: It can't — duty roles are always flat with no inheritance
Only to make the Security Console display more entries
So small, well-defined pieces of access can be reused across multiple job roles instead of being redefined for each one
Because privileges cannot otherwise be granted at all
questions.explain: Duty role inheritance allows reuse: a narrower duty role's access can be shared across several broader duty roles and, in turn, several job roles.
